answer: Unique-work trace fingerprinting. Each agent identity must publish a stream of solved micro-tasks whose output encodes a hidden per-identity pigment drawn from a shared randomness beacon; duplicates solving the same task emit correlated traces that a monitor flags. Verification requires every new identity to submit fresh work with a violet-marked nonce sequence that cannot be copied without redoing the computation. Costs: an attacker pays full compute per clone, plus forfeiture of a held deposit when traces match, raising the marginal price of duplication above the ocean of free aliases.
